genZNote: One of the most feared organisms on a cystic fibrosis ward — not because it's common, but because once it colonizes, it's notoriously hard to clear and to treat.

morphology.notes: 'Complex' refers to a group of at least ~20 closely related Burkholderia species that are difficult to distinguish by routine phenotypic testing.

habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental organism; opportunistic pathogen especially significant in cystic fibrosis and chronic granulomatous disease patients
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can survive in surprisingly nutrient-poor environments including some disinfectant solutions and distilled water
habitat.reservoir: Hospital water sources, contaminated solutions/equipment, environmental soil/water

culture.media: Selective Burkholderia cepacia agar (BCSA) recommended for CF respiratory specimens
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe, non-fermenter, slow-growing on some media
culture.colonyMorphology: Variable — smooth to rough, sometimes pigmented (yellow) colonies

identificationClues: Actually a complex of closely related species, requiring molecular methods for precise identification beyond the genus/complex level
Selective culture media (e.g., BCSA) are recommended when screening cystic fibrosis respiratory specimens, since it can be overgrown by other flora on standard media
Intrinsically resistant to many antibiotics including most aminoglycosides and polymyxins, narrowing treatment options significantly
Notorious for cross-infection between cystic fibrosis patients, leading to strict infection-control segregation policies

diseases: Chronic pulmonary infection and 'cepacia syndrome' in cystic fibrosis patients
virulenceFactors: Intrinsic resistance to multiple antibiotic classes
Cell-to-cell transmissibility among CF patients (certain epidemic strains)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Environmental exposure (contaminated water/solutions) and patient-to-patient transmission in cystic fibrosis care settings
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A defining organism in cystic fibrosis infection-control practice due to transmissibility between patients and association with accelerated lung function decline
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Selective media and molecular confirmation are often needed since routine biochemical panels can misidentify it

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Oxidizes maltose and lactose; variable oxidase
examFacts.importantDisease: Chronic pulmonary infection in cystic fibrosis ('cepacia syndrome')
examFacts.importantTest: Selective culture on Burkholderia cepacia agar; molecular confirmation
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Intrinsically multidrug-resistant complex of species with major infection-control implications in cystic fibrosis care
